### David and Ahimelech
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/david-and-ahimelech
Passage: 1 Samuel 21:6
Points:
- David fled from King Saul to Nob, seeking food and assistance from the priest Ahimelech.
- Although the consecrated bread was legally reserved for priests, Ahimelech understood that preserving human life takes priority over ceremonial ritual.
- Jesus later cited this event to demonstrate that fulfilling human need supersedes rigid religious traditions.
- Faithful obedience requires honoring the spirit of God's law rather than prioritizing ceremonial form over mercy.
- Knowing how to apply God's commandments properly requires regular prayer and study of Scripture in Christian community.

### Day 26: 1 Samuel 21:1–9
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-26-1-samuel-21-19.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 21:4
Points:
- Fleeing for his life, David turned to the tabernacle at Nob to be near those who served God.
- David's request for five loaves anticipates Christ's miraculous feeding of the multitudes in the Gospels.
- The Bread of the Presence was a lasting sign of God's covenant faithfulness to His people.
- Receiving the holy bread assured David of the Lord's sustaining presence throughout his exile.
- For believers today, Jesus is the true Bread of Life whose abiding presence never leaves or forsakes us.
